A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CarGait and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material. All 13 pages of each version support comparison, including relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original gait-recognition experiments, re-ranking comparisons, ablations, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–6 and the supplementary figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds independently trained SwinGait-3D results, verification measurements, and architectural ablations in Tables 7–9.

M1.justification: The bidirectional strip-wise cross-attention, residual connections, ranking and classification losses, and re-ranking procedure are unchanged. Additional head/block configurations are ablations, not revisions to the proposed default architecture.

E1.justification: Gait3D, GREW, and OU-MVLP remain the datasets. Section 10 adds identity verification under a fixed false-positive constraint on Gait3D, extending evaluation beyond ranked retrieval. Additional SwinGait-3D configurations reuse existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds an evaluated SwinGait-3D initial-model baseline on OU-MVLP, where its v1 Table 1 entries were absent. The KR, LBR, GCR, and binary-classifier comparisons in existing experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added verification experiment uses top-1000 candidates and TPR at FPR=0.01, separately from the retained top-10 retrieval protocol. v2 also evaluates independently trained SwinGait-3D checkpoints and additional attention-head/block configurations. Existing splits and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 11 and Table 9 add sensitivity tests with 4 or 16 attention heads and 2 or 4 blocks, compared with the default 8 heads and one block. Existing loss, training-baseline, candidate-list, and runtime analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added tables continue to report point estimates only.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–6 and plotted results are unchanged. Table 7 adds independently trained SwinGait-3D results, including GREW Rank-1 of 78.7 before and 79.5 after re-ranking; these do not replace v1's cited 79.3 baseline under identical conditions. Table 8 adds verification gains across seven models, including GaitSet's 27.1 to 39.3, and Table 9 adds architectural sensitivity results.

T1.justification: The feature-space definitions, distance formulation, and losses in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptable cross-attention re-ranking and improved recognition across models and datasets. The rewritten contribution bullets restate existing claims rather than changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that its independently trained GREW model does not reproduce the cited scores. It also explains verification's relevance under strict false-positive constraints and interprets the new architectural ablations as showing limited sensitivity to head/block counts.

D1.justification: Section 7 replaces the 7.92 MB inference-memory statement with parameter counts: 2.07–9.21 million trainable parameters and at most 0.4 million at inference. Section 9 identifies OpenGait as the implementation used for the independently trained checkpoints. Existing hardware and training-time information is retained.

R1.justification: The same 57 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Additional citations reuse existing references without changing CarGait's positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the contribution bullets, adjusts the ablation transition, renames the runtime section, and adds supplementary Sections 9–11. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–9, moves the unchanged Figure 9 from page 12 to page 13, and rearranges appendix text. Figure 1's caption now identifies its datasets. All nine figure images and existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 7–9 modestly strengthen empirical support by filling missing model settings, testing verification, and examining architectural sensitivity. Checkpoint provenance, the reproduction caveat, and parameter counts improve transparency. These gains outweigh the loss of the earlier memory-use figure, while the method and established results remain unchanged.
